A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a high rate of de novo dolichyl phosphate biosynthesis in MDA231 breast cancer cells leads to an efficient N-linked glycosylated translocation of IGR-1R to plasma membrane, and thereby to an extracellular autocrinic IGF-1 signaling.

a low expression of IGR-1R at cell surface of estrogen independent breast cancer cells is not due to a lack of the IGF-1 receptor but rather to an insufficient de novo synthesis of the dolichol phosphate.
dolichyl phosphate regulates IGF-1 receptor function in breast cancer cells by modulating the intracellular and extracellular IGF signaling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of dolichylphosphate synthesis may regulate the transition between the intracellular and the extracellular IGF pathway.
the level of dolichyl-phosphate in breast cancer cells is an important regulator of cell growth and that this regulation can be manipulated by the addition of exogenous dolichyl phosphate.
the low expression and/or function of IGF-IR in breast cancer cells is not due to the lack of ligand binding or receptor activation, but rather to the lack of cell surface receptor expression.
